text:
maria: quick onboarding check for asteria-13b — CI lint flagged a tokenizer/context mismatch and runtime couldn't locate weights. pinging @ken and @ash for asset/serve defaults :wave:

ken: on it. which path did you point to? I can also re-run the lint.

maria: gs://redwood-models/asteria/13b/v1/weights.tar.gz — agent logs showed 404 from storage and lint output included: 
```
ERROR: config-lint: missing field `tokenizer.pad_id`
ERROR: config-lint: tokenizer.vocab_size (50280) != tokenizer.weights_vocab (50256)
WARNING: config-lint: context_pad (0) < recommended default (16) for attention optimizations
ERROR: runtime: weights not found at gs://redwood-models/asteria/13b/v1/weights.tar.gz
```

ash: :eyes: that vocab mismatch is odd. sometimes upstream packs special tokens differently and shifts subtoken ids. did the publisher include a tokenizer.json or separate merges.txt?

maria: they uploaded tokenizer.json but it has fields: 
```json
{"vocab_size":50280, "bos_token_id":1, "eos_token_id":2}
```
no pad_id, no merges.txt.

ken: ok - two things: 1) our config-gate expects either `pad_id` or `use_special_token_pad: true` to allow implicit padding; otherwise lint fails. 2) weights path 404 — storage team might have CASE mismatch. @sam can you check permissions and exact object key?

sam: checking now. listing bucket... hmm object exists at `gs://redwood-models/asteria/13b/V1/weights.tar.gz` (capital V). runtime fetch uses case-sensitive keys, so that'll 404. reuploaded a lowercase symlink/manifest; CI re-run queued.

ci-bot: re-run triggered by sam — lint job #8421 in queue.

ash: for tokenizer: if upstream omitted pad_id, our onboarding flow usually sets `pad_id = eos_token_id` by default for causal models, unless the manifest explicitly requests no-pad. but that defaulting happens in the onboarding script only if `defaults.apply_missing_token_ids: true` in config.json. right now their config.json doesn't opt-in.

maria: ah — should we set that default automatically for hosted onboarding? avoids a lot of tiny PRs.

cj: i'd prefer being explicit in the repo. automatic defaults can mask real issues. proposal: onboarding pipeline will auto-suggest `pad_id` in the candidate config and create a small PR that authors must ack. separate flag `onboard.auto_patch_allowed` would control auto-merge for trusted publishers.

ken: +1 to PR suggestion flow. For now to get smoke serving we can patch the config in-tree with a comment: `# set pad_id to eos for causal fallback` and add `context_pad: 16` to match our runtime kernel selection.

maria: copying the suggested minimal patch here so I can push quickly: 
```json
{
  "model_name": "asteria-13b",
  "tokenizer": { "vocab_size": 50280, "bos_token_id": 1, "eos_token_id": 2, "pad_id": 2 },
  "serve": { "context_window": 32768, "context_pad": 16 },
  "assets": { "weights_uri": "gs://redwood-models/asteria/13b/v1/weights.tar.gz" }
}
```

ash: that should silence the lint about pad_id and give the runtime the pad to use for batching. also sets context_pad so the kernel chooser will pick the tiled attention path.

sam: weights object key fixed, CI passed the re-run lint job: 
```
ci-bot: lint#8421 PASSED (warnings: tokenizer.vocab_size vs weights_vocab mismatch persisted — needs follow-up)
```

maria: thanks. i'll open the PR with the minimal patch and link to this thread. follow-up ticket to sync tokenizer files from publisher and reconcile vocab count.

cj: please include in PR description: steps to repro the 50280 vs 50256 mismatch, and add a QA checklist for downstream evals.

maria: will do. resolving for now — tagging for visibility @eng-ml :white_check_mark:
